terms.gloss: a maker, a craftsman who makes things
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.150: opificēs omnēs in sordidā arte versantur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: One who makes a work (opus + facere): a workman or artisan, and in Cicero the maker of the world (N.D. 1.18). Latin usually names the maker with a relative clause: who made this machine?, quis hanc māchinam fēcit?.

terms.gloss: the works, the firm that makes something
evidence: Suet. Gram. 23: officīnās prōmercālium vestium, workshops making clothes for sale (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BC 1.34: officīna armōrum, an arms works (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A workshop or manufactory (Lewis & Short; see factory): where the maker is a firm, name its works, ex quā officīnā?, which manufacturer?

evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.120: fabricātor minūtōrum opusculōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Rare (Lewis & Short), always with the genitive of what was made; in Vergil the maker of the wooden horse.

evidence: M-O s.v. manufacturer, after Egger, with a query on domus

sources: Lewis & Short: opifex · Lewis & Short: officina · Lewis & Short: fabricator
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. manufacturer.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
